s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of altered mental status, fever, flaccid paralysis, and respiratory failure with evidence of disseminated infection and multi-organ involvement
key_facts: Patient is around 60 years old
Patient lives in a rural area in the southeastern US
Patient has a history of porphyria with polyneuropathy
Patient has a history of alcohol use disorder
Patient has a recent diagnosis of hyper-IgE syndrome
Patient was taking oral prednisone before admission
Patient presented with fever
Patient has respiratory failure with lower lobe nodules and a left lower lobe infiltrate
Bronchoalveolar lavage revealed Aspergillus fumigatus, Candida spp, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa
Autopsy findings showed disseminated aspergillosis and candidiasis without ocular involvement
Multiple organ involvement including lungs, liver, pancreas, colon, appendix, and kidneys

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of altered mental status, fever, flaccid paralysis, and respiratory failure with evidence of disseminated infection and multi-organ involvement

Patient lives in a rural area in the southeastern US
Patient has a history of porphyria with polyneuropathy

Patient has respiratory failure with lower lobe nodules and a left lower lobe infiltrate
Bronchoalveolar lavage revealed Aspergillus fumigatus, Candida spp, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa
Autopsy findings showed disseminated aspergillosis and candidiasis without ocular involvement
Multiple organ involvement including lungs, liver, pancreas, colon, appendix, and kidneys

differentials: Acute flaccid paralysis due to West Nile virus
per_call: Acute flaccid paralysis due to West Nile virus

raw.rationale: The presence of larval sections in the eyes, specifically the focal eosinophil-rich inflammatory infiltrate with a cross-section of a possible degenerating larva in the posterior choroid of the right eye and a coiled, incompletely sectioned filariform larva within a medium-caliber artery, strongly supports the diagnosis of cysticercosis, which is caused by the ingestion of tapeworm eggs.

rejected.label: Disseminated aspergillosis
rejected.why: Although autopsy findings showed disseminated aspergillosis, the key finding of larval sections in the eyes points towards a parasitic infection like cysticercosis.

rejected.label: Pseudomonas aeruginosa sepsis
rejected.why: Pseudomonas aeruginosa was found in the bronchoalveolar lavage, but it does not explain the presence of larval sections in the eyes.

rejected.label: Disseminated candidiasis
rejected.why: Like aspergillosis, candidiasis was found at autopsy, but it does not account for the larval sections in the eyes.

rejected.label: Toxocariasis
rejected.why: Toxocariasis could explain some findings, but the specific description of the larvae and their location in the eyes, along with the clinical context, makes cysticercosis a more fitting diagnosis.
